en: The Praise of Śiva as the Destroyer of Poverty:
To the Lord of the Universe, the savior from the ocean of hell, the nectar for the ears, and the wearer of the crescent moon upon his crest.
Salutations to Śiva, who is white with the luster of camphor, who wears matted locks, and who is the fire that consumes the suffering of poverty;
salutations to the beloved of Gaurī, who wears a digit of the moon.
To the one who is Time and the Ender, whose bracelets are the lords of serpents;
to the bearer of the Gaṅgā, the crusher of the king of elephants;
to the one for whom devotion is dear, the remover of the fear of the disease of worldly existence.
To the fierce one, who carries across the difficult ocean of existence; to the one composed of light, whose body is the beautiful dance of qualities and names; [to the one who destroys] poverty...
To him who wears garments of skin, who is smeared with the ashes of the dead,
whose forehead has an eye, who is adorned with jeweled earrings, whose pair of feet is graced by anklets, who bears matted locks— to him, [the destroyer] of poverty...
To the five-faced one, adorned with the king of serpents, clad in golden raiment, the ornament of the three worlds,
the bestower of boons upon the ground of bliss, and who is composed of darkness— to him, [I offer] poverty...
To the beloved of the Sun, the one who ferries beings across the ocean of existence,
the ender of Time, worshipped by the Lotus-Seated One;
to the Three-Eyed One, marked with auspicious characteristics, [salutation] to the destroyer of poverty...
To the beloved of Rāma, the bestower of boons upon the Lord of the Raghus, the beloved of the serpent-king, the deliverer from the ocean of hell,
who is filled with merit among the meritorious, worshipped by the gods, [and the remover of] poverty...
To Mukteśvara, the bestower of fruits, to Gaṇeśvara,
who is fond of song, whose vehicle is the lord of bulls (Vṛṣabha), who is clothed in the skin of an elephant, to Maheśvara— to [him] for the removal of poverty... 8.
This hymn composed by Vasiṣṭha wards off all diseases,
swiftly bestows all prosperity, and increases one's sons and grandsons.
He who recites it daily at the three junctions of the day shall indeed attain heaven.
Thus ends the "Hymn for the Destruction of Poverty" composed by the venerable Vasiṣṭha.
